constraints.text: Constraint for whatever fix comes out of this: ConnectionPool.__init__ and AsyncConnectionPool.__init__ keep their public signature and defaults (max_connections=10, max_keepalive_connections=None, ...), and handle_request / handle_async_request stay unchanged.

decisions.text: Decision: every connection the pool holds, idle keepalive ones included, counts toward max_connections. At the cap a request for a new origin has to reuse or evict an idle connection rather than exceed the cap.

next_action.text: Next step, not started: fix the create-new-connection branch in _assign_requests_to_connections in httpcore/_async/connection_pool.py, then regenerate the sync file with scripts/unasync.py and rerun the visible test.

reality.text: The create-new-connection branch only counts connections that are not idle, so idle keepalive connections never count toward max_connections and the idle-eviction branch below it is never reached.

ruled_out.text: Mock backend is fine: every connect_tcp gets a fresh stream over its own copy of the buffer, and a finished request leaves its connection IDLE in the pool as it should. Ruled out as the cause.

Single thread, no concurrency, and it still over-creates: a and b are IDLE, c gets a brand new connection, 3 held with max_connections=2. Nothing can lose a wakeup here, so the lock and synchronization are ruled out.
Rejected the Redis counter. httpcore is a single-process client library, the cap is per pool, and a network service dependency is out of scope for a pool fix.

unknowns.text: Also noticed: the keepalive cleanup loop uses len([connection.is_idle() for connection in self._connections]), which counts every connection, not only idle ones. Odd, but not this bug. Not touching keepalive cleanup or _max_keepalive_connections; out of scope.
